newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mostly higher, retailers gain.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mostly higher, retailers gain.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mostly higher in sluggish trade in which gains included leading retailers, the country's second largest bank and brewing giant Bavaria.

Medellin's general price index edged up 0.12 percent to close at 17,309.88 on trading volume of about 1.8 billion pesos. Bogota's closed up 0.41 percent at 1,130.27, meanwhile, on extremely thin volume of just 797 million pesos. "The markets were very weak today," said a trader added he thought potential investors were holding back pending a possible cut in domestic interest rates.
A drop in rates would take some of the premium off investment in Colombia's active fixed-income market.

Friday's winners included Cadenalco, which added 1.14 percent in Bogota to close at 880 pesos per share after it reported a 20 rise in its first-quarter net early in the day. The company, Colombia's top retailer in terms of overall sales and size, gained 1.40 percent in Medellin where it ended at 872 pesos per share.
Cadenalco's top competitor, Carulla, led gains. It rose 5.26 percent in Medellin, ending at 3,500 pesos per share on market talk that it too had a strong first quarter.
Blue-chip Bavaria rose 1.29 percent in Bogota and 1.26 percent in Medellin, closing on both exchanges at 7,950 pesos per share, on follow-through buying after its sharp run-up earlier this year.

Banco de Colombia, the country's No. 2 bank, eked out its first sizeable gain since last Friday, meanwhile, when it began trading lower on news that its talks to forge a strategic partnership with Spain's Banco Central Hispano-Americano had collapsed. Colombia ended up 1.33 percent in Bogota at 380 pesos per share, still well below book value.
